content: For fixed positive integer k satisfying x^2+y^2=k(xy+1), choose a positive solution minimizing max(x,y), with x>=y. The other root z=ky-x of T^2-kyT+(y^2-k) is integral. Product xz=y^2-k. If z<0, then k-y^2=x(-z)>=x=ky-z>=k+1, impossible since y^2>=1. Also P(y)=(2-k)y^2-k<0 for k>=2; because x>y and P(y)=(y-x)(y-z), this forces z<y. Thus z=0 gives k=y^2; z>0 gives smaller positive solution (y,z), contradiction. k=1 is already square.
